newsitem.title: USA: Judge to rule on Hilton motions soon.
newsitem.headline: Judge to rule on Hilton motions soon.

text.p: A federal judge is expected to issue a decision soon on two key motions in Hilton Hotels Corp's $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for rival ITT Corp.

The motions, which seek to prevent ITT from increasing the size of its board of directors or interfering with the board election process, were discussed during an hour-long hearing here Wednesday before U.S. District Court Judge Philip Pro.
Hilton spokesman Marc Grossman said the judge told both sides he planned to issue a ruling shortly.

In January Hilton offered to acquire ITT for a combination of cash and stock worth $6.5 billion. Hilton also offered to assume $4 billion in ITT debt, bringing the total value of the deal to $10.5 billion.
ITT rejected the bid and has embarked on a program to shed non-core assets in an effort to raise cash and perhaps offer shareholders a special dividend.
Hilton, which has proposed 25 nominees to ITT's board, is asking the court to prevent ITT from increasing its board beyond the current 11 directors.
If the judge rules in Hilton's favor, the company stands a better chance of getting sympathetic directors on ITT's board, something Hilton will need if ITT continues to oppose a merger.
The Beverly Hills, Calif.-based hotel and gaming giant is also trying to prevent ITT from adopting a poison pill, which would make a takeover more expensive.
In a separate motion, Hilton has asked the court to force ITT to hold it annual meeting in May. The judge is expected to hear arguments on this motion later.
